title: Pulsewire handovers — weekly SRE update (Oct 19 2028)
content:
TL;DR:
- Quiet week overall: no sev1, two sev2 incidents (KV cache mismatch + routing flaps), several low-latency regressions tied to a new batching heuristic.
- SLOs: token-gen availability steady at 99.93% (weekly rolling, target 99.9%), p95 latency drifted 60ms above target during peak on Wed night.
- Handoffs: improved checklist tested; still inconsistent ownership on cross-team alerts (routing vs serving).

Incident summaries (short):
1) KV cache mismatch — Oct 17 03:20 UTC — Sev2 — 45m mitigation
   - Symptoms: increased model cold starts for specific conversational sessions; KV cache lookups returning nulls for ~2% of requests to prod-gpu-region-3.
   - Impact: p50->p95 latency skewed, some 500s from model-serving layer. Customer-facing errors bubbled for ~10 customers (minor rate).
   - Root cause (investigation): rollback of a cache key hashing change in dev inadvertently rolled into canary config; mismatch between compile-time key format and stored keys across nodes after a staggered restart.
   - Mitigation: forced eviction + full rehydrate of prefix cache across region and reverted canary flag.
   - Action items: (a) add a small e2e for cache key format in our integration tests (owner: Ava), (b) add a safety gate preventing config changes that change key schema without migration path (owner: Ravi), (c) document cache rehydrate runbook gap (owner: Sofia).

2) Edge routing flap — Oct 18 21:10 UTC — Sev2 — 20m mitigation, intermittent errors following overloaded edge-proxy autoscaling loop
   - Symptoms: sudden spike in 502/503 responses from edge-proxy; autoscaler thrashing between scale-to-zero and scale-to-2 on a small subset of hosts.
   - Impact: brief per-route error increases, fallback to alternative region succeeded for critical customers.
   - Root cause: autoscale cooldown misconfigured after recent autoscaler refactor; combined with a bad healthcheck for native 'streaming' route.
   - Mitigation: disabled new cooldown logic, forced fixed-min of 1 for affected pool, patched healthcheck to better reflect streaming readiness.
   - Action items: (a) add chaos test to exercise cooldown behavior under bursty traffic (owner: Liam), (b) update autoscaler config templates (owner: infra team).

SLO snapshot and observations:
- Token generation availability (global) — weekly rolling: 99.93% (target 99.9%) — PASS but margin tightened.
- p95 latency (global, last 7d): target 220ms, observed 280ms peak on Oct 17-18 window. Root causes linked to KV rehydrates + batching heuristic change.
- Error budget consumption this sprint: ~0.03% used (within plan), but risk on high-traffic accounts during peak hours noted.

On-call handoff notes (what the next shift should know):
- Follow-ups from KV cache incident: rehydrate verification still in progress for region-3; check /ops/cache-rehydrate/status and confirm no resurface events for 24h (owner: Ava).
- Watch the autoscaler metrics for edge-proxy pools 7/8 between 20:00-02:00 UTC — recently added fixed-min is temporary. If thrash reappears, escalate to infra lead and flip cooldown to legacy mode.
- Batching heuristic A/B experiment (batcher-v2) toggled in canary; metrics dashboard: batch-size, token-cost-per-call, p95-latency. Canary on 5% traffic. If p95 increases >40ms for two contiguous hours, rollback immediately.
- Recent alert sigs: alert A-ERR-STREAM-2 still noisy; temp suppression planned after tuning threshold.

Runbook and tooling gaps identified:
- No automated migration workflow for cache key schema changes — currently manual and error prone.
- Rehydrate visibility: /ops/cache-rehydrate page lacks per-prefix timeline and owner tagging.
- Healthcheck semantics for streaming routes not well-documented (leads to autoscaler surprises).

Operational action list (prioritized):
1) Short (24-72h): implement cache-key format e2e test + add config safety gate (Ava, Ravi) — target: Oct 25.
2) Medium (1-2 weeks): autoscaler cooldown test harness + update templates (Liam, infra) — target: Nov 2.
3) Medium: add per-prefix rehydrate timeline and owner meta to ops dashboard (Sofia) — target: Oct 30.
4) Longer: migrate batching experiments into rollout pipeline with automatic rollback on latency regressions (owner: eng-platform) — planning session next Thursday.

Notes for leadership / cross-team asks:
- Product: we need to freeze any key-schema-affecting experiments until migration plan exists — request a short pause on related PRs.
- Support: prepare a short comms note template in case KV regression resurfaces; keep it ready in /templates/incidents.

Meeting snippets / decisions this week:
- Handoff checklist iteration accepted: added explicit "who will run the rehydrate" line and a quick verification check at T+1h. Will try this for two weeks then reassess.
- Agreed to run a weekly 30-min ops grooming with infra and serving runtime to triage runbook gaps — Friday mornings 09:30 PT.

Quick wins and wins-to-share:
- Canary rollback pattern reduced blast radius on the KV issue — canary metrics and a quick revert saved ~2 hours of customer impact.
- Improved runbook link discoverability in Slack via the new /ops-runbook bot command (SRE-tools).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we enforce a config gate for all key-schema changes at the CI level or handle case-by-case? (Decision needed by Oct 26).
- How aggressive should we be with batcher-v2 rollout given small but measurable latency impact? Proposal: slow ramp + automatic rollback threshold.

Next week's priorities:
- Finish cache-key e2e + safety gate.
- Autoscaler cooldown harness initial prototype.
- Run the new handoff checklist across two on-call rotations and capture feedback.

Attachments / links (operational):
- Incident timeline (raw notes): https://docs.internal.redwood/incident/INC-3471/timeline
- Runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/cache-rehydrate
- Dashboards: ops.dashboard.redwood/sre/pulsewire

Notes to self / messy scribbles (keep informal):
- Confirm if the canary rollback logs captured the exact moment key format mismatch happened — I think yes but need PR trace.
- Double-check that the streaming-healthcheck change didn't ship with unrelated refactor (saw a small PR that touched both).
- flag: remind product about pause on schema-affecting experiments Monday morning standup.

If anything urgent surfaces while I'm offline Sat-Sun, ping on-call Slack channel and tag @ravi.
